title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This playbook codifies Redwood Inference's standard processes and expectations for hiring, employee onboarding, performance cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for people-ops, hiring managers, and anyone acting as a people manager. Follow these procedures to ensure consistent candidate experience, predictable ramp, and fair performance reviews.

Sections
1) Hiring process and role lifecycle
2) Candidate experience and interview rubric
3) New hire onboarding checklist (first 90 days)
4) Performance and feedback cycle (annual + midcycle)
5) Manager responsibilities and calibration
6) Templates and examples

1) Hiring process and role lifecycle

Purpose: provide a repeatable, auditable flow from requisition to offer acceptance.
Owner: people-ops (requisition approval), hiring manager (role definition & interview loop), recruiting (sourcing & screening).

Key steps (timeline targets in parentheses):
- Role definition & hiring plan (1 week): hiring manager completes Job Requisition Form and rubric in Greenhouse. Include must-have skills, preferred skills, mission-fit criteria, interviewers, and target compensation band. People-ops approval required for all external hires.
- Sourcing & screening (2-4 weeks): recruiter screens, runs phone screen, and submits candidate brief to hiring manager.
- Interview loop (1-3 weeks): structured loop with 3-5 interviews depending on level; at least one cross-functional interviewer and one bar-raiser. Use standardized rubrics.
- Debrief & decision (48 hours after last on-site/loop): hiring manager convenes debrief, collects scores, documents decision rationale in Greenhouse. People-ops reviews for equity checks if needed.
- Offer & negotiation (48-72 hours): recruiter drafts offer using compensation bands and equity guidelines. Offer approval required from hiring manager + finance for above-band hires.
- Acceptance -> background checks -> onboarding kickoff: recruiter schedules start-date, sends welcome pack. People-ops triggers IT and manager onboarding tasks.

Hiring controls and guardrails
- All roles must have a documented hiring rubric before interviews begin.
- Salary band must be confirmed with People Ops and Finance; exceptions need VP People Ops approval.
- Interview feedback must be submitted within 24 hours of interview.
- For executive-level hires, involve Head of People and at least one executive sponsor.

2) Candidate experience and interview rubric

Interview loop components (default for IC roles):
- Phone screen (30m): recruiter + hiring manager quick screen for fit, interest, logistics.
- Technical/role screen (45-60m): assess core skills; use a live exercise or take-home as defined in the rubric.
- System design or strategic interview (60m) for senior roles.
- Team/collaboration interview (45m): culture & cross-team collaboration.
- Hiring manager interview (30-45m): alignment to role, career path, manager style.

Rubric (submit numeric 1-5 and short notes):
- Problem solving / technical skill
- Product sense / domain knowledge
- Communication & collaboration
- Ownership & execution history
- Culture add / mission alignment

Bar-raiser guidance
- Bar-raisers focus on long-term potential and raise the overall standard. They can veto a hire when serious concerns on technical or behavioral fit exist; scope and use of veto is documented in the debrief notes.

3) New hire onboarding checklist (first 90 days)

Goal: reduce time-to-contribution; ensure compliance, culture fit, and clarity of expectations.
Owners: People Ops (IT, benefits), Hiring Manager (role-specific ramp), Buddy (peer collaborator).

Day 0-7: pre-boarding and first week
- IT provisioning: laptop, access to Slack, Google Workspace, Redwood Console (dev/test) and SSO (owner: IT: target 3 business days prior to start).
- Paperwork: sign offer, complete tax forms, e-sign NDAs and code of conduct, benefits enrollment window explained.
- Welcome email & schedule: recruiter sends first-week schedule and onboarding plan.
- First day 1: team welcome, intro to company mission, short product overview (30m), and 1:1 with manager to set first-week goals.

Week 2-4: functional onboarding
- Role training: complete role-specific training doc and read key repos/docs. Manager should provide 30/60/90-day goals.
- Buddy program: assigned buddy meets 3x first two weeks to answer practical questions.
- Small project: assign an initial low-risk project with clear success criteria to enable early wins.

Month 2-3: ramp & clarity
- Ongoing feedback: weekly 1:1s; manager provides written progress note at 30 and 60 days.
- Performance check-in at 90 days: formal written check-in in Lattice (or People Ops tool) covering core competencies, strengths, and development plan.

Onboarding checklist table (columns: task | owner | target)
- Complete pre-boarding forms | recruiter | before day 1
- Laptop & SSO access | IT | day 1
- Slack & internal tools access | IT | day 1
- Security training & data handling policy review | Security | day 7
- First 30/60/90 goals set | manager | day 7
- Compliance & benefits enrollment | People Ops | day 14
- 90-day review | manager & People Ops | day 90

4) Performance and feedback cycle

Principles
- Continuous feedback over once-a-year surprises.
- Calibration to reduce bias and ensure equitable standards.
- Development-focused reviews with clear behaviors and outcomes.

Cadence and artifacts
- Weekly 1:1s: manager & direct report; capture notes in the template on Confluence.
- Quarterly check-ins: light written update + goals progress.
- Annual review (timeline: Oct-Nov): self-review, manager review, peer feedback, calibration.
- Mid-cycle review (April): focused calibration for promotion pipeline and compensation planning.

Evaluation dimensions (standardized):
- Impact & delivery
- Technical craft or role-specific skills
- Collaboration & communication
- Ownership & leadership (scope varies by level)
- Growth & learning orientation

Rating scale guidance (recommended):
- 5 = Outstanding (consistently exceeds expectations; promotable)
- 4 = Exceeds expectations (often delivers above bar)
- 3 = Meets expectations (solid contributor)
- 2 = Needs improvement (clear gaps; development plan required)
- 1 = Unsatisfactory (serious concerns; performance improvement plan may follow)

Performance improvement process (PIP)
- Trigger: consecutive check-ins showing sustained rating 2 or documented material performance problems.
- Steps: manager documents concerns, creates a 60-90 day PIP with measurable goals, People Ops reviews and provides legal/HR guidance, weekly manager check-ins documented, end-of-PIP decision documented and reviewed by VP People Ops.

Calibration and equity
- Calibration meetings convened by People Ops for each function before final ratings are locked. Include cross-functional managers and HR partner. Document justification for outlier ratings.

5) Manager responsibilities and calibration

Manager playbook (core expectations):
- Hire responsibly: complete rubrics, timely interview feedback, and prioritize candidate experience.
- Ramp: prepare 30/60/90 plan, assign buddy, and provide repeated feedback.
- Development: run career conversations twice per year, create Individual Development Plans (IDP) for directs.
- Feedback & performance: give timely corrective feedback, document concerns; run check-ins and complete review artifacts on schedule.
- Compensation & promotion: gather evidence for promotions, prepare promotion packet per Promotion Guidelines doc, and escalate to committee when needed.

Manager checklist (first 90 days of a new direct):
- Week 1: 1:1 to set priorities, walk through goals, intro to team values.
- Week 2: assign first project and clarify success metrics.
- Week 4: 30-day written progress note.
- Week 8: 60-day feedback summary.
- Week 12: 90-day review & development plan.

Calibration meeting process
1. People Ops schedules functional calibration meetings (2-3 weeks before rating lock).
2. Managers submit rating proposals and evidence in the Confluence calibration packet.
3. Cross-functional discussion to align on level expectations; People Ops flags anomalies and equity concerns.
4. Final ratings locked and recorded in HRIS.

6) Templates and examples

Included templates (links to Confluence pages):
- Job Requisition Form template (link: /confluence/templates/job-requisition)
- Interview rubric template (link: /confluence/templates/interview-rubric)
- 30/60/90 plan template (link: /confluence/templates/30-60-90)
- 90-day review form (link: /confluence/templates/90-day-review)
- Promotion packet checklist (link: /confluence/templates/promotion-packet)

Sample manager email for new hire first day:
"Hi team \u2014 please join me in welcoming [Name], starting today as [Role]. They will be onboarding with [Buddy] and working on [Project]. Please add them to relevant Slack channels and help them settle in."

Hiring metrics and KPIs (tracked by People Ops)
- Offer acceptance rate (target >= 70%)
- Time to fill (requisition opened -> offer accepted; target median <= 30 days)
- Time to productivity (time to reach expected contribution; target median <= 90 days)
- Diversity pipeline metrics: percentage of underrepresented candidates at each funnel stage
- Interview feedback completion rate (target 95% within 24 hours)

Change management and exceptions
- Changes to this playbook must be approved by Head of People (owner) and documented in the revision log below.
- Exceptions (e.g., accelerated hiring, remote country payroll setup) require written sign-off from People Ops and Finance.

Revision log:
- 2024-03-15: Playbook created by Ava Martinez (People Ops).
- 2025-09-20: Added bar-raiser guidance and updated time-to-fill target.
- 2026-01-10: Published updated onboarding checklist and performance calibration timeline.

Appendix: Quick checklists
- Hiring manager quick checklist: post job -> finalize rubric -> schedule interviews -> debrief in 48h -> submit offer decision.
- New hire first week checklist: hardware, access, intro to team, first project, benefits enrollment.
- Manager monthly checklist: 1:1s, progress notes, career conversation scheduling, review artifacts.
